boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Chustenahlah record (December 26, 1861) in Operations in the Indian Territory [November-December 1861]. Stand Watie's December 27 pursuit and Cooper's scout to the Kansas line are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names McIntosh's and Douglas Cooper's brigades with no figures; the live field reads zero; the frozen description says McIntosh left Fort Gibson with 1,380. McIntosh says he came to Fort Gibson with 1,600 and marched with a force of 1,380, that the enemy was estimated at 1,700, and that Stand Watie's 300 arrived as the battle ended. Cooper says McIntosh announced he would take the field with some 2,000, and that his own column had not arrived: he heard of the attack the next morning.
claims.rationale: Column figures and an estimate of the enemy; by both reports Cooper's column was not engaged, although the frozen force field names it. No account by Opothleyahola's side was inspected; every figure for his force and losses is an opponent's estimate or a history's. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Colonel James McQueen McIntosh and Opothleyahola. McIntosh sent Griffith to the right and Young to the left and says the Seminoles were led by Halek Tustenuggee. Cooper says McIntosh pushed on without waiting even for Stand Watie, calls this precipitancy, and argues the chief could have been captured had McIntosh waited for Cooper's column.
claims.rationale: Cooper's criticism is his own interested judgment, not an established causal finding. No automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown; the live field reads 251 (US 211; CS 40). McIntosh says the enemy's killed were upwards of 250 and his loss 8 killed and 32 wounded, but his closing line reads 'Killed, 0; wounded, 40' in OCR; he captured 160 women and children (read '1G0') and 20 negroes. Cooper says Stand Watie's pursuit next day killed 15 without loss.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The basis of the live US 211 is not established in the selected passages.

open_questions: The regimental reports Nos. 11-15 (W. C. Young's No. 11, printed after McIntosh's, was read while delimiting and not selected), Stand Watie's and Boudinot's reports, returns and maps remain deferred. Britton's chapter XIII covers Chustenahlah but was not selected for this record: the three-family ceiling was taken by the two commanders' reports.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. McIntosh's January 1, 1862 report is an interested Confederate account. Cooper's January 20, 1862 report covers all three engagements and is an interested Confederate account; it is written after McIntosh's January 1 report and criticizes McIntosh. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
